item.text: The research itself is progressing, but persistence is still the hard blocker: command execution cannot access the workspace. I’ve also found a useful contrary/exculpatory integrity item—Tshisekedi’s August 2023 instruction to address IGF-reported state-enterprise mismanagement—while preserving the limitation that this is a formal response, not proof of personal integrity or successful enforcement. I’m making one direct patch attempt now so the manifest is not left stale if the file-edit channel is available independently.

The workspace remained inaccessible: both shell reads and `apply_patch` failed at sandbox initialization (`RTM_NEWADDR`), so `research-ledger-manifest.json` could not be updated. I completed the available continuation research and provide manifest-ready additions below.

New defensible units:

- `WEB-051` — AU, 27 June 2023: Tshisekedi participated in the Luanda quadripartite summit; the communiqué commended his commitment to dialogue and adopted coordinated peace-process timelines. Maps 2B.1/2B.7, 8B.1/8B.9. [AU communiqué](https://www.peaceau.org/en/article/communique-quadripartite-summit-of-the-east-african-community-economic-community-of-central-african-states-international-conference-on-the-great-lakes-region-and-southern-african-development-community-under-the-auspices-of-the-african-union-27-june-2023)

- `WEB-052` — IMF fifth review, 20 December 2023: security and elections drove spending reprioritization; fiscal, depreciation, and inflationary pressures remained high, while authorities committed to reforms, efficiency, governance, and transparency. Maps 5B.3/5B.7/5B.9, 8B.6–8B.8. [IMF report](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2023/12/19/democratic-republic-of-the-congo-fifth-review-under-the-extended-credit-facility-542654)

- `WEB-053` — U.S. State Department 2023 human-rights report: credible reports covered government killings, torture, life-threatening prison conditions, arbitrary detention, weak judicial independence, corruption, and restrictions under the state of siege. Administration-level evidence only; no personal order inferred. Maps 3B.1/3B.4/3B.5/3B.10, 4B.4, 7B.6/7B.7. [Report mirror](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2107668.html)

- `WEB-054` — Actualité.cd, 19 July 2023: the Court of Accounts challenged BCECO’s attempt to avoid IGF control over PDL-145T and emphasized the program’s substantial public expenditure and audit risks. Maps 5B.5–5B.7, 7B.6, 8B.5–8B.8. [Report](https://actualite.cd/index.php/2023/07/19/rdc-la-cour-des-comptes-enjoint-le-bceco-de-retirer-sa-note-dinformation-adressee-aux)

- `WEB-055` — Actualité.cd, 27 August 2023: Tshisekedi responded to IGF findings on state-enterprise mismanagement by directing ministers to improve governance and address auditor inaction. This is a direct corrective instruction, but not evidence of successful enforcement or personal integrity. Maps 5B.5/5B.7, 7B.2/7B.6/7B.8, 8B.6/8B.8. [Report](https://actualite.cd/2023/08/27/gouvernance-des-entreprises-publiques-felix-tshisekedi-sindigne-de-linaction-des)

- `WEB-056` — UNICEF, 4 September 2023: approximately 27 million children were enrolled, nearly 7 million were out of school, and over 800,000 children had been displaced while more than 2,000 eastern schools closed because of insecurity. Maps 3B.7, 6B.2/6B.3/6B.6/6B.10, 8B.7. [UNICEF release](https://www.unicef.org/drcongo/communique-presse/rentree-scolaire-2023-2024)

- `WEB-057` — UNICEF, 13 May 2023: after Kalehe floods killed over 400 people, UNICEF delivered WASH, health, child-protection, and education assistance, while documenting destroyed houses, schools, and health facilities. Maps 6B.6/6B.8/6B.10, 8B.9. Shared humanitarian attribution; not direct presidential conduct. [UNICEF release](https://www.unicef.org/drcongo/en/press-releases/unicef-responds-deadly-floods-kalehe)

- `WEB-058` — Presidency of DRC, 5 September 2023: Tshisekedi personally launched free maternity and newborn care, specified covered services, and set national-expansion objectives. Use as official corroboration of WEB-045, not as an independent source family. Maps 5B.1/5B.6/5B.8, 6B.1–6B.4/6B.8, 8B.1/8B.2. [Presidency release](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_president_felix_tshisekedi_lance_officiellement_la_gratuite_de_la_maternite_et_la_prise_en_charge_du_nouveau_ne_a_kinshasa)

Manifest dispositions:

- Add `WEB-051`–`WEB-058` as `final_evidence`, except `WEB-058` may be marked `context` if duplicate-source policy prevents a second official maternity unit.
- Add the previously rejected Republic of Congo World Bank economic update as `rejected`: wrong country, not DRC.
- Keep IMF numeric snippets and World Bank poverty-PDF snippets as `discovery_only`; the IMF HTML review itself is now usable through `WEB-052`.
- Keep 2023 asset-declaration and family-enrichment searches as `rejected/no_usable_candidate`; no defensible personal-integrity finding emerged.

Chapter status:

- **2B:** materially improved through AU diplomacy and IMF security/fiscal context; proxy-command evidence remains unresolved.
- **3B:** materially improved with an accessible national human-rights report; prison and torture evidence remains administration-level.
- **4B:** no major new attribution breakthrough; CENI and observer limitations remain as previously documented.
- **5B:** materially improved through IMF findings and an opened PDL-145T audit-resistance report.
- **6B:** materially improved through UNICEF education, disaster-response, and direct maternity evidence; mortality, learning, sanitation, and durable social-protection outcomes remain sparse.
- **7B:** no adverse personal-nexus evidence found; `WEB-055` is limited contrary/exculpatory evidence of formal anti-mismanagement response.
- **8B:** materially improved across diplomacy, macroeconomic management, PDL execution, education disruption, disaster response, and maternity implementation.

No score or ranking judgment was produced.
